public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Asymptotics of subsets of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ with integer average

Number of nonempty subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \dots, n\}$ whose elements have an integer average.

Benoit Cloitre conjectured the asymptotic expansion:
$$a(n) = \frac{2^{n+1}}{n} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n} + \frac{3}{n^2} + \frac{13}{n^3} + \frac{75}{n^4} + \frac{541}{n^5} + o\left(\frac{1}{n^5}\right)\right)$$
where the coefficients $1, 1, 3, 13, 75, 541, \dots$ are the Fubini numbers (preferential arrangements, A000670).

*References:*
- [A051293](https://oeis.org/A051293)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
- [A000670](https://oeis.org/A000670)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA51293


open Polynomial

open scoped Topology

open Finset Nat Real Filter Asymptotics

/--
Number of nonempty subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \dots, n\}$ whose elements have an integer average.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.card (
    (Finset.Icc 1 n).powerset.filter fun S : Finset ℕ =>
      S.Nonempty ∧ S.card ∣ S.sum id
  )

def aReal (n : ℕ) : ℝ := a n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 5 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 8 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 15 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) = 2^{n+1}/n \cdot (1 + 1/n + 3/n^2 + 13/n^3 + 75/n^4 + 541/n^5 + o(1/n^5))$. - _Benoit Cloitre_, Oct 20 2002

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/51293.wip.lean#L503"]
theorem tendsto_aReal_asymptotic :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      (aReal n - (2 ^ (n + 1) / (n : ℝ)) *
        (1 + 1 / (n : ℝ) + 3 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2 + 13 / (n : ℝ) ^ 3 + 75 / (n : ℝ) ^ 4 + 541 / (n : ℝ) ^ 5)) /
      (2 ^ (n + 1) / (n : ℝ) ^ 6)) atTop (nhds 0) := by
    sorry

end OeisA51293

reformulations.difference: The source writes the remainder as o(1/n^5) inside the factor 2^(n+1)/n. Lean instead asserts that the absolute remainder, divided by 2^(n+1)/n^6, tends to zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let B(n)=2^(n+1)/n and P(n)=1+1/n+3/n^2+13/n^3+75/n^4+541/n^5. For n≥1, set r(n)=aReal(n)/B(n)−P(n). Then aReal(n)=B(n)(P(n)+r(n)), and (aReal(n)−B(n)P(n))/(2^(n+1)/n^6)=r(n)/(1/n^5). Thus the Lean limit is exactly r=o(n^−5). The division-by-zero convention at n=0 cannot affect the limit. This equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real sequence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review51293.statements_equivalent, with no sorry dependencies.

review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. Lean computations for n=1,…,12 match the OEIS table, including all five test lemmas; a(0)=0 and the empty subset is excluded. Also proved that, for a nonempty finite subset, the natural-number divisibility condition is equivalent to having an integer-valued real average. OEIS and the cited paper corroborate the research-solved status. OEIS entry pages were Cloudflare-blocked, so their official data mirror was used. The public APN proof has matching definitions and target and no explicit proof holes; its rebuild against the current toolchain encountered legacy API incompatibilities, so an independent certification of that external proof is not claimed.
